thread:
alex: Heads-up — saw repeat latency spikes in eu-central after a bunch of handoffs from shared -> reserved slices around 09:12 UTC. Patterns look like egress queues backing up during the slot seal window.

maria: Ugh, saw that in graphs. 99p token latency jumped ~180ms for a subset of tenants. Any noisy neighbor signal?

alex: Not classic GPU noisy neighbor (no memory pressure) — it's more network egress tails. When we seal a slot to hand it off to a dedicated slice, the proxy routes briefly pile up and we see microburst egress.

kevin: Do we have a dashboard link?

alex: https://dash.redwood/internal/egress?range=1h&cluster=eu-central — filter tenant=prod-*. Look at proxy_out_queue and per-route bursts.

jamal: ops-bot flagged 5 alerts: proxy_queue_depth > 400 for >2m on 3 nodes. ops-bot: alert:proxy_queue_depth - triggered at 09:14:22 UTC :point_up:

nora: Could this be the slot sealing window (the 12s grace) where we drain but still accept in-flight requests? If so we might need hedged routing during seal.

maria: Agree. Current seal semantics: mark slot draining, wait 12s, handoff. That drain window is too blunt for egress-limited tenants.

alex: Proposed play: implement "egress-hedge" during seal — for the 8s core of the seal window, route new traffic for high-egress tenants to a warmed reserved fallback *and* allow in-flight small fanout to finish on original slot with lower priority. Hedged path costs more (extra hop) but avoids tail latency.

kevin: Sounds reasonable. Cost question — how much extra egress we expect? Rough calc?

alex: Rough numbers: for top 20 tenants, hedging adds ~10-15% extra egress for the seal duration. Given seals are ~1% of slot events overall, net monthly egress delta ~+3-4% for those tenants.

jamal: Can we make it opt-in per-customer? customers with strict latency SLOs can enable hedging. Also fallback to non-hedge if we hit total egress budget.

nora: Implementation notes: scheduler needs a new seal state + egress tag propagation; routing layer needs to consult tenant hedging flag and warm fallback pool. We'll also need a short-lived slot-snap token so we don't double-bill requests in observability (and to avoid duplicate byte counts).

kevin: Observability change: tracing needs a new tag "egress.hedged=true|false" and metrics to record extra bytes + extra tokens generated. Also must show hedged vs non-hedged p99.

maria: If we do opt-in, support team will need to explain cost tradeoff to customers. Could we add a budget cap per tenant to auto-disable hedging if egress > X?

alex: Yes — implement soft budget enforcement: when tenant_egress_30d > budget_threshold then switch hedging to fallback=false. We'll surface via billing report.

jamal: Quick probing plan before rolling: 1) simulate seal traffic via load-test on staging (reuse slot-seal harness), 2) run 1% canary in eu-central for 24h, 3) measure p99 and egress delta.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist: [ ] api change (routing), [ ] scheduler change (seal state), [ ] metrics + trace tags, [ ] docs + runbook update, [ ] billing flag.

nora: Can someone run the quick query to get baseline egress per-seal event? e.g.:

  SELECT
    seal_id,
    SUM(bytes) as bytes_during_seal,
    COUNT(request_id) as reqs
  FROM ingress_events
  WHERE cluster = 'eu-central' AND time BETWEEN now()-1d AND now()
  GROUP BY seal_id
  ORDER BY bytes_during_seal DESC
  LIMIT 50;

maria: I'll run that and paste results in #eng-infra after lunch.

kevin: One more thought — we should consider a slot-seal "stagger" to avoid simultaneous seals in same AZ; that might reduce aggregate egress spikes. Low-effort mitigation before hedging lands.

alex: Good call. Stagger + hedging opt-in seems like the plan. I'll open an RFC with implementation details and cost estimate.

jamal: +1. If we can keep the canary to <5% extra egress at fleet scale, ops is comfortable.

nora: I'll draft the runbook updates for hedged handoff and the abort conditions.

alex: thanks — assigning tasks in RFC. cc @kevin @maria @jamal. :thumbsup:
